turns.text: Hey, are you free for a minute? I need help choosing what to do this weekend.
I am. Is this a real decision, or are you asking me to help you avoid your errands?
It can be both. I have laundry, groceries, and a pile of things I said I would sort out.
Then let’s plan something small so the whole weekend doesn’t disappear into chores.
That sounds good. I was thinking we could try that new cafe near the bookshop.
The one with the plants in the window? I’ve walked past it a few times.
Yes. Their menu looks nice, and they have a little patio at the back.
A patio would be lovely if it isn’t too hot. What time were you thinking?
Maybe Saturday around one, before it gets busy.
One works. I can meet you by the bookshop, and we can walk over together.
Perfect. I should probably do the grocery shopping in the morning first.
Make a list before you go, or you’ll come home with snacks and forget the actual groceries.
That happened once. I bought three kinds of biscuits and no cooking oil.
It happened last month. You called me from the shop asking what you needed.
All right, I’ll write everything down this time. Do you want anything while I’m there?
Could you get tea if you see the ginger kind? I’m almost out.
Sure. I’ll send you a photo if I’m not sure which one you mean.
Thanks. And don’t rush through your chores just to get out the door. We can meet a little later if you need to.
I appreciate that. I’ve been trying to make every free hour productive, and it’s getting tiring.
A quiet lunch and a walk count as a good use of the day too.
You’re right. Maybe after lunch we can browse the bookshop without buying anything.
Without buying anything? That sounds ambitious for both of us.
We can look. Whether we leave empty-handed is a separate question.
Fair. I’ve been meaning to find a novel for the train anyway.
What are you in the mood for? Something funny, or something mysterious?
A mystery, as long as it isn’t so complicated that I need a notebook to follow it.
I know exactly the kind. I’ll show you one I finished last week.
Great. Then lunch, a little browsing, and no pressure to hurry home.
That sounds like the sort of Saturday I need.
It’s a plan, then. Saturday at one by the bookshop.
Saturday at one. I’ll message you when I’m heading out.
Sounds good. I’ll see you then, and I’ll bring my recommendations for the mystery shelf.
Excellent. Now I’m going to write that shopping list before I forget why I opened my notes app.
Put ginger tea on it first. That way at least one of us gets what they need.
Done. Talk to you later, and thanks for helping me plan a proper day off.
Anytime. Have a restful evening, and I’ll see you Saturday.
